draft.title: Reception, transduction and transmission
card: Reception
a sense receptor detects a stimulus from the environment, such as light, sound or pressure. Each type of receptor responds to one kind of energy.
Transduction
the receptor changes the stimulus energy into electrical impulses. The nervous system can only work with electrical impulses, not with light or sound itself.
Transmission
the electrical impulses travel along neurons to the brain. This is how the information leaves the sense organ and reaches the brain.
The order is reception, then transduction, then transmission. The brain only works on the information once it arrives.
draft.remember: Detect the stimulus, change it into electrical impulses, then send the impulses to the brain.

a.q: In the eye, receptors change light energy into electrical impulses. Which process is this?
opts: Transduction
Reception
Transmission
Interpretation
a.why: Changing one form of energy into electrical impulses is transduction. Reception is only the detecting of the light, and transmission is the later trip of the impulses to the brain.
a.clue: Which step changes the form of the energy?

b.q: Sam touches a hot mug. Receptors in his fingertips detect the heat, then change it into electrical impulses. What must happen next for him to feel the heat?
opts: The impulses travel along neurons to the brain
The receptors detect the heat for a second time
The heat is changed into electrical impulses again
The impulses stay in the fingertips until they fade
b.why: Reception and transduction have both happened, so the next step is transmission. The impulses must travel along neurons to the brain. Transduction cannot happen again, because the heat has already been changed into impulses.
b.clue: Two steps are done. Which step is left?

b.best: The impulses travel along neurons to the brain

problems.detail: The why says transduction 'cannot happen again' because the heat has already been changed into impulses. This is false: receptors keep detecting and transducing for as long as the stimulus lasts. The option is wrong because it is not the next step, not because it is impossible.

'The nervous system can only work with electrical impulses' oversimplifies. Neural signalling is electrochemical, and neurons pass signals across synapses with chemical neurotransmitters. VCE texts describe the signal as electrochemical or neural impulses, so 'only' could mislead students later in the course.
The distractors are weak. 'Stay in the fingertips until they fade' and 'changed into electrical impulses again' are easy to rule out without knowing the idea, so the question is easy for Year 11.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer and agree with the card. The why for (b) wrongly says transduction cannot happen again, and the card's claim that the nervous system 'can only' use electrical impulses glosses over the chemical part of neural signalling.

proposal.title: Reception, transduction and transmission
card: Reception
a sense receptor detects a stimulus from the environment, such as light, sound or pressure. Each type of receptor is specialised to respond to a particular kind of stimulus.
Transduction
the receptor converts the stimulus energy into neural impulses, which are electrochemical signals. Neurons can carry these signals, but they cannot carry light or sound itself.
Transmission
the neural impulses travel along neurons from the sense organ to the brain. This is how the information reaches the brain.
The order is reception, then transduction, then transmission. The brain can only interpret the information once the impulses arrive.
proposal.remember: Detect the stimulus, convert it into neural impulses, then carry the impulses to the brain.

opts: Transduction
Reception

Interpretation

b.q: Sam touches a hot mug. Receptors in his skin respond to the heat and convert it into neural impulses. What must happen next, before his brain can interpret the heat?
opts: Transmission of the impulses along neurons to the brain
Interpretation of the impulses by the brain
Reception of the heat by receptors in the skin
Transduction of the heat into neural impulses
b.why: The receptors responding is reception, and converting the heat into impulses is transduction, so the next step is transmission to the brain. Interpretation is tempting, but it cannot happen until the impulses have reached the brain. Reception and transduction keep going while Sam touches the mug, but they are not the next step.
b.clue: Responding and converting are done. How does the signal reach the brain?

b.best: Transmission of the impulses along neurons to the brain
